title: The Thundershroom That Tripled
story: In the storm-swamp of Hollow Reek grows Murrabel, a mushroom-beast who booms with thunder whenever she is struck. Mr 6 has seen the warning carved on a stump: every strike makes each Murrabel split into three. He sits down on a log to think before lifting his sword even once.
question: There is 1 Murrabel now, and each strike triples the number of mushroom-beasts. If Mr 6 struck 4 times, then a wandering druid turned 20 of the mushroom-beasts friendly, how many Murrabels would still be booming?
solution: Each strike triples the count: 1 → 3 → 9 → 27 → 81 after 4 strikes.
The druid turns 20 of them friendly: 81 - 20 = 61.
So 61 Murrabels would still be booming.
praise: Tracking the tripling strike by strike was exactly the right method — the last move was simply taking the druid's 20 away from 81.
hint: Multiply by 3 once for each strike, writing the number after every strike — then handle the druid's 20 at the very end.
victory: Mr 6 calculates 61 booming mushrooms, sheathes his sword, and simply offers Murrabel an umbrella instead. She blushes pink, stops thundering, and the swamp hears birdsong for the first time in years.
imagePrompt: A huge purple storm-cloud mushroom crackling with tiny lightning in a misty swamp, with a numeral-six knight sitting thoughtfully on a log doing sums on a slate instead of attacking.
